subject.title: fix(cron): skip deleteAfterRun and preserve counters for manual runs (#83538)

question: Should OpenClaw define manual `openclaw cron run` completions as non-consuming verification/debug runs that do not delete one-shot jobs, advance retry/backoff counters, or emit failure alerts?
rationale: The patch is a coherent fix for the reported data-loss path, but it intentionally changes compatibility-sensitive cron state and notification semantics for existing operators.

options.title: Accept Non-Consuming Manual Runs
options.body: Merge this direction after exact-head checks are green, making scheduled timer execution the only path that consumes `deleteAfterRun`, retry/backoff, and failure-alert state.

options.title: Narrow To Delete Preservation
options.body: Ask for a smaller patch that only prevents manual `deleteAfterRun` consumption while preserving more of the previous manual counter or alert behavior.

options.title: Reject The Contract Change
options.body: Close or pause this PR and document that destructive manual runs are intentional, leaving this issue's preferred behavior unimplemented.

recommendation.title: Accept Non-Consuming Manual Runs
recommendation.body: Merge this direction after exact-head checks are green, making scheduled timer execution the only path that consumes `deleteAfterRun`, retry/backoff, and failure-alert state.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent cron service and schema history makes this the strongest available routing candidate for the cron behavior contract decision.
